justification: B fills pages evenly: its body text runs continuously across pages B2 and B3, with running headers and numbered headings. A leaves large empty gaps. A1 ends with a big blank area, and A3 is mostly empty after a short section. A's brighter blue band and divider rules are attractive, and its looser line spacing is comfortable. But the page breaks are choppy and the rhythm is uneven. B's headings are clear and its darker band is more restrained.

A sets section headings (1 نسبه, 2 طفولته, 3 ترحاله) as bold, numbered, and clearly separated from the body (A4, A5), so the sections are easy to scan. B has no section headings in the body, only plain, lightly marked ones (B4, B5), and its text runs on more densely. A's contents page is numbered to match the sections (A2). A's sans-serif Arabic text is clear, and its navy cover has a visible accent rule (A1), where B's rule is barely visible against the green (B1). B's running headers and page numbers are fine but less informative.

B has a table of contents (B2), running headers and numbered headings (B3-B7), and a consistent text rhythm. A has plain text with unclear heading hierarchy, an abrupt cut after the first paragraph, and thin rules (A2-A5). B's cover is a deeper, more refined navy (B1). Both show broken image placeholder text, but A's is more prominent.

A uses a full-width green band for the section heading 'التسمية' on A3, which gives a clear break and stronger hierarchy. B only sets small numbered headings inline (B3, B5) that barely stand out from the body text. A's serif Arabic text has slightly looser leading. The cover pages and the image page are similar in both. B's numbering and 'n / 6' footers are tidy, but its headings are weaker.

B has a cover, a table of contents (B2), numbered section headings and a thin running header rule. Together these give clearer navigation and hierarchy. Its text pages (B3-B6) have slightly airier margins and consistent line spacing. A has a dark header band on its text pages, which is a nice touch. But its dense, cramped first page (A2) has no section headings, and its headings are small (A3, A4). B's TOC page is mostly empty, which is a minor drawback.

B has larger, easier-to-read body text with comfortable line spacing and fuller pages. Its running headers and footers add navigation, and the page 3 flow is more continuous. A's text is smaller and denser with wider measure, and A2 leaves a large gap at the bottom. A's blue band and heading hierarchy are clear, but B's green band is similarly effective and the overall B pages are more cohesive.

Design A has a serif Arabic face with tighter line spacing and a green title band. Its running headers and footers on pages 2 and 3 help navigation, and the text blocks are compact and readable (A1, A2). Design B's sans typeface is cleaner and more modern, with generous leading and a dark navy band (B1). The heading sizes in B are clear. B's text flows across pages 2 and 3, filling page 2 fully, so page 3 is less empty than A's. A's page 3 breaks off early and leaves a large blank area (A3). B's pages are more evenly filled (B2, B3). A's headers and footers are a plus, but B has the better overall rhythm.

A has a table of contents (A2), running headers and footers with page numbers, and section headings that are clearly set off (A4, A5). B has no contents page and no running header. Its section headings are plain and small (B3, B4), and its last page is nearly empty (B5). A's cover is a deeper navy with a crisper title (A1 vs B1). A's TOC page is mostly empty, but this is a minor flaw. A's body text is a bit larger and more legible.

B has a table of contents page (B2) and a running header band with a consistent rule and running titles (B3-B7). Its body text carries full diacritics and is set at a comfortable size. Its section heads are bolder and clearer (B4, B5). A's pages (A2-A5) have no header band and no TOC. Its text blocks are dense, and its section heads are weaker. Its blue cover is attractive, but B's cover is more consistent with the rest of the document. B's TOC is sparse, with the page numbers misaligned from the labels.

B has a full-width green band behind the section heading (B3), running headers and a clear footer, and a more legible, looser serif body. A's pages are dense with tight leading and no header. A also integrates the image better with text on A5, whereas B leaves B5 and B6 half empty after pushing the image onto its own page. Overall B's hierarchy and finish are stronger, but B's pagination is weaker.

B is the more polished and consistent of the two: its navy running header band on B2 and B3 and its rules above the section titles give a clear rhythm. Its body text is a bit larger with comfortable leading. A's bold section numbers give some hierarchy, but its thin running header is weak. A also has an awkward gap on A1 and tighter, denser text on A2.

Design B has larger, more readable Arabic text with comfortable line spacing and pages that fill evenly, with text running to the bottom of pages 2 and 3. Design A's text is small and dense, and it leaves big empty areas on pages 1 and 3 (A1, A3). A's page 3 is mostly blank because the section break comes early. A's bright blue header band is bolder, but B's dark navy header is calmer and fits better with the body. B's heading hierarchy is clear and its pagination is better.

A has a dark header band with running titles and a filled section band for "التسمية" (A3), so sections are easy to find and the page numbers read clearly. Its heading sizes are also more distinct. B runs the text on with only thin rules and small headings (B3, B4), so it is flatter. B places the image inline after the text (B5), which is better integrated. A isolates the image on a mostly empty page (A6), which wastes space. Overall A's structure and hierarchy are stronger.

A uses a serif Arabic face with lighter, more elegant headings and clear rules above sections. Its running header and footer are cleaner and carry a page number. B uses a sans face with bold digit-prefixed headings ("1 منشآت", "2 كيفية") that look awkward in RTL. Its text is slightly denser, and the "2 / 3" footer is odd. Both title bands are similar, with a green band in A and a navy band in B.

A uses a serif Naskh face with tighter, more even text blocks and section headings, and its running headers and footers carry the section name. Its TOC page numbers match the actual pages (4, 4, 5, 5, 5). B's geometric sans Arabic is less traditional and looser, and its TOC says 6 for two sections whose headings fall on pages 5 and 6 (بسكرة and فاس both sit on page 6, so those entries are fine, but the sans body is less comfortable to read). B also ends on a mostly empty page 7 holding a few orphaned lines. A's dark green cover is rich, though B's navy cover is similarly solid.

B adds a table of contents (B2) and sets its headings off with clearer spacing (B4-B6). A has tighter, denser text and no contents page (A2-A5). A's header band is fine, and its dark navy cover (A1) is slightly richer than B's. B's text is looser and more readable, though its last page is mostly empty (B7).

Design B is more compact, with a dark header band on every page and bold section headings (B3, B4) that keep a consistent rhythm. Design A has a mostly empty contents page whose page numbers sit far from their entries (A2), and it repeats a thin header rule on each page with no band. Its text is denser with tighter margins (A3). B's heading style is clean and its body text is comfortable to read, though A's heading numbering is a small plus.

B is more compact and consistent: the dark navy banner sits well with a heading and a running header on pages 2-3, and the text flows across pages without wasted space (B2, B3). A has a vivid blue band and a clear heading hierarchy, with a mixed serif subtitle (A1). However, its body text is small with loose leading, and page 3 is mostly empty because the text breaks early (A2, A3). B's text is larger and justified, which improves readability, though its lines are tighter and the heading is slightly less distinct.

A has a dark navy cover with a clear title block, a table of contents page, running headers and footers with page numbers like '3 / 7', and bold numbered section headings (A3, A5, A6). B has no TOC, and its headings are small and light, so sections blend into the body text; it also has a lighter, flatter cover (B1) and sparse footers. A's section headings give clearer structure, though its TOC page is mostly empty and its raw image markdown appears awkwardly at the top of A5.

A uses dark navy header bands and section banners (A3, A4) that give clear hierarchy and structure. Its running header is a navy bar and its body text is evenly justified. B has a mostly empty contents page (B2) and plain headings run into body text (B3). B's text is dense but readable. Both have broken image placeholder text (A4, A6, B5, B7).

Design A uses a looser line height and a larger, more airy text size. Its cover band is dark navy with a clear title, and the second page has a thin top rule, which gives a consistent rhythm. Its body text is more readable, and the paragraph spacing is clearer. Design B is tighter and denser, with smaller text and cramped paragraph spacing on B2. B3 is mostly empty at the bottom. B does add running headers with section names, which are helpful, but its overall reading comfort is lower than A's.

B has navy header bands on section titles (B3, B4), a running header and a page counter, so the hierarchy is clear. Its text is evenly justified and the lines are well spaced (B2, B3). A shows only thin rules and plain headings (A2, A4), with a flatter hierarchy. A's body text is denser and its page tops are more crowded, and a broken image placeholder appears on both designs. A's cover is fine, but B's deeper navy and cleaner type look more polished.

Design A has a lighter, more refined Arabic typeface with clear heading sizes and a rule above each section heading (A1, A2, A3). The header band on A2 and A3 carries the section title, and the pages feel more structured. Design B's headings carry numerals (1, 2, 3) and the body text looks tighter and heavier. B also has no rules above headings and only a thin line under its running header (B1, B2, B3). Both leave a large empty area on the last page.

A uses a serif-like Arabic face with generous leading and open line spacing, so the body text reads comfortably (A2, A3). Its section band on A3 is a bold green with white title, and the thin header rule and light running header are refined. B's body text is denser and set in a heavier sans face. B's heavy navy header bar and the boxed section title on B3 look blunt, and the text blocks are cramped. The images are equivalent in both designs (A6, B6), and the covers are comparable.

A has a clear table of contents (A2), running heads naming each section, and bold numbered headings that break up the body (A3, A5, A6). Its type is a readable Arabic face with consistent page numbers. B has a striking band-style section divider (B3), but it leaves the page half empty. B's body pages carry unnumbered headings with weak contrast, and the stray leftover text on B5 leaves that page mostly blank. B also has no table of contents. B's cover is darker and plainer than A's navy cover with accent line (A1). Both designs carry the same raw image-markdown artifacts.

A has clearer hierarchy: numbered section headings (1 التسمية, 1.1 العصر الفرعوني) and running headers with rules on A3-A5. Its looser line spacing and more open paragraphs read comfortably, and the dark cover on A1 is strong. Its weakness is the image on A6, which sits alone on a page with a large empty lower half. B packs the text densely and the headings are weak (B3, B4). B does integrate the image with the text on B5, which gives a more balanced page, but its paragraphs are cramped and the cover is plainer.

A uses navy header bands for section titles and running headers on each page, so the sections are easy to find. Body text is dense but evenly spaced, and the pages are consistently filled. B has a divider page with a sidebar and large title, which adds some variety. But B has no running header and only a thin top rule. Its page 5 is mostly empty, and its section headings are weak plain text. The B divider page also takes up a page without adding content.

B has a header bar, a filled band behind the section heading (B3), and a dedicated section heading with a page-total footer, giving clearer hierarchy and navigation. B's body text is also vowelled and set with generous leading, though the image page B6 is left mostly empty. A's text is dense and edge-to-edge, the heading on A3 is only a rule and plain text, and the image is placed after a short text block on A5, which is better integrated, but overall A looks less structured.

B has a table of contents (B2), running headers, numbered section headings inside the text, and a page counter, so the document is easy to navigate. B's body text is clean and consistent. A has a striking divider page with bands (A3) and a clean cover. But A's body pages have no headings on the text pages, so the sections run together, and page 5 (A5) is mostly empty with leftover broken image markup. B has the same broken image markup (B5, B7), but it is less obtrusive. The A divider page works as a graphic, but A overall lacks the navigation and hierarchy that B has.

A uses larger body text with generous leading and clear heading sizes, so it reads more comfortably (A1, A2). Its page 1 fills the page well and the dark navy header band looks restrained. B has small, dense text, a large empty lower half on page 1 and a mostly empty page 3, so it feels unbalanced (B1, B3). B's brighter blue band is bolder but less refined.

A has larger, more legible Arabic text with a calm navy header band and a clear heading hierarchy. Its running header bars on A2 and A3 add polish, and its paragraph rhythm is steadier. B's text is smaller with very loose line spacing, and its bright blue band with a serif subtitle clashes with the Arabic. B's headings are weaker, and the paragraph that runs across B2 into B3 breaks awkwardly. A's page 3 is mostly empty, but so is B's.

B has a deeper navy cover and a running header band with the title and section name on every page. Its section headings are clearer, and page numbers read 'n / 5'. Its body text is more continuous: text flows across pages and fills them, and the last page is mostly full. A has a plain body, a nearly empty page 5 after a break, and a small, tight, hard-to-read body font. A's headings are weaker and it has no header bands.

B uses dark navy banner headings and a header bar, which give clear section markers (B3, B4). B also has no near-empty contents page, and its text flows continuously. A's table of contents page is mostly blank, with page numbers detached from the entries (A2). A's headings are plain and its body text is slightly denser and less airy. Both show the same broken image-markdown text.

A uses a geometric Arabic sans with clear section headings (نسبه, طفولته, بسكرة, فاس) that stand out from the body, and its TOC page numbers match the sections. B runs the sections inline into dense text with small headings, and its page header and footer are cluttered. B's green cover is attractive, but A's navy cover and top rule are consistent with its interior. A has a near-empty last page, which is a minor flaw.

B's text reads well with comfortable line spacing and fully justified lines, and its thin rules separate sections, but the page-2 heading is not very prominent and its dark-navy top band is repeated on every page. A's numbered headings (A1, A2) are bolder and give clearer hierarchy, plus it has a running header and page numbers; however, its page 3 is half empty and its tighter, denser text is harder on the eye.

A sets section titles in dark navy banner bands (A3, A4) and adds a running header with the title and section name on each page (A2-A6). These give clear hierarchy and navigation. B uses plain heading text with a thin rule (B2, B4) and only a footer, so headings are weaker and the pages look flatter. Both keep the same dense body text and show the same broken image markup. A's text is slightly heavier and easier to read, and its cover is more polished.

A uses a sans-serif Arabic face with a navy band, a clear heading hierarchy and a slightly larger body size with comfortable leading (A1, A2). B's serif Arabic is thinner and less crisp at this size, and its green band works about equally well (B1, B2). A's headers and footers, with page numbers like '2 / 3', are tidy. B's footers are fine but its headings are slightly weaker. Both leave the lower part of the last page empty (A3, B3).

B sets the section title "التسمية" in a green band on B3, which gives clear section breaks. Its text is smoother and the page-number footers are centered. In A, the headings are bold, small and close to the body text, so they separate poorly on A3 and A5. A's text blocks are dense and the lines look slightly uneven. The images are about the same in both designs. B's cover uses a muted green with a faint rule. A's navy cover is crisper, but it does not outweigh the body-page advantages.

A uses a serif-like Arabic face with comfortable line spacing and clear headings. Its dark green band is restrained and its running headers and footers are consistent. B has a saturated blue band and looser, lighter text with weaker heading contrast. B's sparse page 3 also begins mid-sentence, which breaks the flow, while A's page 3 starts a fresh paragraph.

B has a running header, page numbers and a table of contents. Its dense, evenly set text runs continuously. Its section headings are numbered, but they sit inline and are not very prominent. A has a cover and then plain text pages with no table of contents. Its section headings are tiny and weak, and the page 5 text ends after a few lines, leaving a mostly empty page. Page 2 of A is a dense wall of text. B is more polished and navigable, though its TOC page is mostly empty and its page numbers do not match.

A uses a clearer, more legible Arabic typeface. Its numbered headings and running headers (A4, A5) make the hierarchy easy to follow. Its table of contents includes section numbers (A2). B's body text is lighter with tighter, harder-to-read line spacing (B3). B's headings are unnumbered and its dark top band is heavy (B3). B's last page is nearly empty, though A's last page is full. B's cover is a dull slate, while A's navy cover is richer (A1). However, A's contents page numbers do not match the actual pages, and B's are closer.

B has a dark cover, a navy top rule on each page, a section-divider page with a TOC band (B3), and larger, more spacious body text with clear section headings (B6). A is denser, with tiny text and no divider structure. It does have a better-looking blue cover, but B's structure and readability win. B does have a near-empty page (B5) and uneven page fill.

A uses a serif Arabic face with comfortable line spacing and right-aligned (ragged) lines, so word spacing stays even. B justifies its lines, which stretches word gaps in places, and its text is tighter. B's navy band and running header bar are crisp and polished, but A's green header band is also clean. A's headings and rules read clearly, and the bullets and paragraph rhythm hold up well. Both leave page 3 largely empty.

A has a green band behind the section heading التسمية (A3), running headers and footers, and looser, more readable line spacing. B has only a thin rule before the heading (B3) and denser text. A's image page (A6) is mostly empty, leaving large whitespace, while B places the image in the text flow (B5), which balances the page better. Overall A's hierarchy and typography are stronger.

Design B has tighter, more refined typography. Its numbered headings, running header and 'n / 3' footer help navigation. Design A has more generous leading and clearer section rules, and its heading sizes make hierarchy clearer. A's page 2 starts with a stray rule and a top blue bar, and its text breaks across pages more awkwardly. A's page 3 also leaves a large empty bottom. A's wider spacing reads comfortably, but B's page 1 balance is slightly cleaner. Overall the two are close, with a slight edge to B for typography and navigation.

B's sans-serif Arabic body text on B3-B6 is cleaner and more legible. Its numbered TOC (B2) and running headers with section names are more useful. Its section headings carry numbers and stand out better than A's headings on A4-A5. A's dark green cover (A1) is fine, but its TOC lacks numbers and its body text is a denser serif-like Arabic with heavy diacritics.

A has a navy header band on the inner pages and a filled navy section band with a white heading ("التسمية") on A3, which gives clear structure. Its "العصر الفرعوني" heading on A5 is also distinct. B has only a thin header rule and small numbered headings ("1 التسمية") that sit inline with body text, so it is flatter and its sections are harder to find. The two images and the cover are comparable, though A's image sits under the header band with more finish. B's text is slightly denser.

A uses a clean sans Arabic face with comfortable leading and a clear dark-blue header band on content pages. Its section heading band (التسمية) is a strong white-on-navy block, and the 'العصر الفرعوني' heading starts a new page so the sections separate cleanly (A3, A5). B's serif Arabic text is denser and slightly tighter. B's green band and heading are fine, but its section heading sits mid-page and the header is a thin line, so it has less presence (B3, B4). The image pages are similar.

B keeps a consistent system: a running header on each page, a navy band behind section titles, and dense pages that run on continuously with page numbers like 2 / 6. A pads the document with a mostly empty divider page (A3) and a nearly blank page (A5) holding only a few lines and a broken image link. A's stronger divider and TOC bands are good design but waste space. B's body text is a touch heavy and crowded, with some broken image links as well, yet its pacing is steadier and its headings are clearer in context.

B adds navy header bands on the interior pages (B3, B6) and a solid navy band behind the section heading (B3). These give a clear structure and tie the pages to the cover. A has only a thin rule, and its headings (A3, A5) are plain bold text, so the section break is weaker. Body text and the image are about equal in both. B's heading treatment gives the pages a stronger rhythm.

B fills pages 2 and 3 more evenly and carries text across the page break, so the page ends and the rhythm stay consistent. A leaves a large empty space on A3 because the section break forces a short page, and it also leaves a gap at the foot of A2. A's body type and line spacing are comfortable, but B's text is similarly legible and its headings are comparably clear. A's header band and running header are slightly stronger, but B's repeated thin top rule is also tidy.

Design A uses a clearer Arabic typeface with proper diacritics and a navy header band on each page with the section name. Its headings (نسبه, طفولته, ترحاله) are visibly larger and set off, so the structure is easy to scan (A3, A4). Design B has a thin, dense font with no header band and no visible heading hierarchy; the headings blend into the body text, and the shaping looks less clean (B3, B4). B's cover is lighter and fine, but A's cover is comparable.

A has a table of contents page, a cover with a thin accent rule, and clear section headings in the body pages (A4, A6). Its text blocks are well spaced with consistent margins. B is more compact, with a header band carrying section names, but it has no TOC and its headings are less distinct, and the pages are dense (B2, B3). B's header band is a plus, but A's structure and clearer hierarchy edge it out. A's last page is mostly empty, and its TOC is sparse.

A has a contents page with dotted-leader rows, running headers and footers with section names, and a clear title block on the dark green cover (A1, A2). Its body type is slightly larger with diacritics and good line spacing (A3, A4). B has no contents page and no running header. Its headings are only slightly bolder than body text, and its text is dense and small, with a mostly empty last page (B2, B3, B5). B's blue cover is fine but offers no advantage.

B has a running header and footer with page numbers, a contents page, and fully vocalised Arabic text, so it reads as a finished book. Its section headings are clearly set off (B4, B5), and the cover is a calm green with a small rule (B1). A has no contents page, only partial running footers, and tighter, denser text with weak headings (A3, A4). A's last page is mostly empty (A5), and its blue cover is fine but plain (A1). B's contents page is mostly empty and its section page numbers look wrong, but it is still stronger overall.

Both share the same layout, but B has a calmer rhythm: thin rules above section headings, lighter heading weight, and slightly more generous line spacing (B1, B2). A uses bold numbered headings and a navy band, which gives stronger hierarchy, but the rules and spacing in B read more cleanly and consistently. A's page 2 header sits tight to the body, while B's footer with a centered page number is tidier (B2, B3).

A has a dark cover with a larger title, a full section-divider page (A3) with a navy band and a contents sidebar, and larger, looser body text with clear paragraph spacing. B is denser, with small justified text and thin rules. Its headings are small and run into the text, and the text is crammed with little breathing room (B2-B5). A has broken image placeholders (A5, A8), but B has them too (B3, B5).

A has larger, more legible body text, bold section numbers and clear headings, plus running headers and footers that help navigation. Its text blocks fill the page well and the paragraph rhythm is steady. B's body text is smaller and tighter, and its headings are lighter and less distinct. B's bright blue band is stronger but starker, while A's navy band is calmer. B also splits a paragraph awkwardly across pages (B2 to B3), and its page 1 leaves a large empty area at the bottom.

B has a clearer typeface, running headers with a rule, numbered section headings (1, 1.1) and comfortable line spacing, so it reads and navigates better (B2-B5). A has dense, tightly spaced text with small footers, and its section headings are less distinct (A2-A4). A places the image inline with its text on A5, which is slightly better integrated. B puts the image on B6 alone with a large empty area below it. Overall B is the more polished and readable document.

Design B is more compact: it has no near-empty TOC page, a bold header band, and body text that flows continuously across pages with section headings (B2-B4). Design A wastes a page on a sparse TOC with a tiny list (A2), and its body text is dense, with narrow line spacing and thin headers (A3-A6). A's green cover is fine, but B's blue cover with its accent rule is comparable. B's text is easier to read and the pages feel more consistent.

A has a dark cover, a table of contents page, a top rule band on inner pages and clear section headings (نسبه, طفولته, ترحاله, بسكرة, فاس) that break up the text. B runs the text as dense blocks with small, weakly differentiated headings and no table of contents, so it has less hierarchy and rhythm. A's text is larger and more comfortable to read, though its last page is mostly empty.

A uses a clean sans Arabic face with a navy running header band and clear section headings (A3, A4), and the cover has a crisp accent rule (A1). Its text is dense but readable, with consistent rhythm. B has a sparse contents page that is mostly empty, and its dotted-row TOC is weak (B2). B's body text is smaller and tighter, and its header is a thin line rather than a band. B's TOC does add navigation, but it wastes the page.

A uses a sans-serif Arabic face with larger, clearer headings and generous line spacing, so the h1/h2/h3 levels are distinct (A1). Its body text is easier to read, and the bullets on A2 are well spaced. B uses a serif face with tighter, smaller text and weaker heading contrast. B does add running headers and footers (B2, B3), but they are cluttered and the layout is denser. Both have a top band on the first page, and both leave a similar amount of blank space at the bottom of page 1.

B reads better. Its body text is a legible, evenly set Arabic face with generous leading. Headings are numbered (1, 2, 3, 3.1) and the TOC carries matching numbers. Running headers show the section name, and the text flows continuously across pages. A has distinct section headings, but its TOC has no numbers and shows wrong page references (6, 6 for the last two entries). Its body text is tighter and denser, and page 7 is nearly empty. A's cover is a plain dark panel, similar to B's.
